title: Nicarao settle the west
description: The Maya-related Nicarao people migrate from the north and settle around the lakes that give the country its name.

title: Gil González explores
description: Gil González Dávila reaches the western valleys and baptises the Nicarao chiefs before being driven out.

title: Granada and León founded
description: Francisco Hernández de Córdoba founds the two cities on the lakes, among the oldest colonial cities in Central America.

title: Momotombo destroys León
description: An eruption of Momotombo buries the old capital, and the city is refounded on its present site.

title: León uprising
description: The citizens of León overthrow the Spanish intendant, the first stir of independence in Central America.

title: Independence
description: Nicaragua secedes from the crumbling federation and becomes an independent republic in its own right.

title: Greytown bombarded
description: The US Navy destroys the port of Greytown after a diplomatic incident, one of the first American military strokes in Latin America.

title: William Walker lands
description: The American filibuster William Walker lands with a handful of mercenaries and within a year is president.

title: Granada burned
description: As the allied Central American armies close in, Walker's men burn Granada to the ground.

title: Walker surrenders
description: Walker surrenders to the allied armies and is deported; his filibuster war becomes the national myth of resistance.

title: Treaty of Managua
description: Britain ends its protectorate over the Mosquito Coast in exchange for a self-governing Mosquito Reserve.

title: Mosquito Coast incorporated
description: President Zelaya's troops seize Bluefields and abolish the Mosquito Reserve, ending the Atlantic coast's autonomy.

title: Marines land
description: Two thousand US Marines land at Bluefields, beginning twenty-one years of almost continuous intervention.

title: Bryan–Chamorro Treaty
description: The treaty sells the United States perpetual rights to build a canal and lease islands in Nicaraguan territory.

title: Pact of Tipitapa
description: The Liberal rebels accept an American-brokered truce to end the civil war; only Sandino refuses to sign.

title: Sandino assassinated
description: The guerrilla hero who fought the Marines is murdered at dinner by the National Guard on Somoza's orders.

title: Somoza dynasty begins
description: Anastasio Somoza García is sworn in as president, beginning a family dictatorship that lasts forty-two years.

title: Somoza shot
description: The poet Rigoberto López Pérez shoots Somoza García at a party; the dictator dies days later, but his sons take over.

title: FSLN founded
description: In exile, Carlos Fonseca and a few students found the Sandinista National Liberation Front, named after the murdered hero.

title: Managua earthquake
description: An earthquake destroys the city and kills at least ten thousand; Somoza keeps much of the relief money, feeding anger for the rising.

title: The publisher is murdered
description: The assassination of the newspaper editor Pedro Joaquín Chamorro detonates the general strike and the insurrection against the dictatorship.

title: Contra war begins
description: Ronald Reagan authorises secret American funding for the Contra rebels, opening a decade of war against the Sandinista state.

title: World Court ruling
description: The International Court of Justice rules that the United States broke international law by mining Nicaragua's harbours and funding the Contras.

title: Sandinistas voted out
description: Violeta Chamorro defeats Daniel Ortega in a surprise free election, ending the Sandinista government and the war.

title: Ortega returns
description: Daniel Ortega is sworn in as president again after sixteen years out of office.

title: Anti-government protests
description: Crackdowns on protests over welfare cuts spiral into a popular revolt that the state suppresses with hundreds of deaths.
